newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish mostly up after quiet day.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish mostly up after quiet day.

text.p: U.S. debt futures finished mostly up on Tuesday after a day of quiet trading bracketed by an early morning high in December U.S. Treasury bonds and another small T-bond rally near the close.
The late rally came on U.S. retail sales data that looked weaker than expected, traders said.
Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc said its Redbook retail sales index fell a seasonally adjusted 0.5 percent for the first two weeks of fiscal November versus October.
Pit traders said they had expected the index to range from up 0.5 percent to down 0.1 percent.
"Johnson Redbook data, which was down a little bit more than expected, generally helped us to finish with a pretty good tone," one trader said.
A midday dip came on disappointment with the U.S. Treasury two-year note auction and initial reaction to remarks by Federal Reserve governor Lawrence Lindsey on inflation, traders said.
The $18.255 billion note auction produced a high yield of 5.662 percent, noncompetitive bids of $928 million and a bid-to-cover ratio of 2.11.
"The 2-year was pretty ugly. The bid-to-cover was weak, the noncomps were extremely weak," one trader said.
In a speech in Washington on Tuesday afternoon, Lindsey said he considered low inflation crucial to home ownership. Minutes later he said he sees continued moderate inflation.
"He made a comment which at first blush looked like he was suggesting there was higher inflation than he had been expecting in the pipeline," a trader said.
"But all he said was that continuing moderate inflation is his expectation. So that was discounted, but it took about 15 minutes to discount," the trader said.
December T-bonds hit an intraday high of 115-12/32 early on U.S. housing starts and chain store sales below expectations.
